transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, nice to meet you too. I came in because... well, it's the people at my apartment. I know they're watching my comings and goings. It's a big brick building, you know, built back in the 70s. My uncle actually used to do bricklaying on places like that. He helped build the old library downtown before they tore it down. Real shame they knocked it down, they had this whole section on old cars I used to look at. 

But anyway... yeah, they're watching me, and they keep slipping notes about me to the front office. I know they are. Everybody keeps telling me, oh, it's just regular notices on the doors, like for the water getting shut off or whatever, but I know what they're really doing. Like this one guy I saw on Tuesday... Tuesday is usually when I go get my groceries because the bus is less crowded, and I like to get those frozen meatloaf dinners, but... yeah, they're definitely slipping notes about me to the office.
During this time, have you had a period when you felt very depressed or unusually high or energized most of the day nearly every day?

Well, I wouldn't say high or energized. I don't really get like that. But depressed... yeah. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day already went bad before I even get my feet on the floor. It's just this weight. My mattress doesn't help either, it's one of those old spring ones. I bought it at a discount place over on 4th Street, you know the one with the big yellow sign? The guy there told me it was firm, but I think he just wanted to make a sale. He had this little dog behind the counter, a terrier mix, I think. Reminded me of a dog I had when I was a kid, Buster. Buster used to chase the mail truck every single day... but yeah, I just feel so down and empty most days.
Have there been times when people were watching you and slipping notes about you even when you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah, actually... there was a spell a little while back. It lasted for several weeks, I think. I wasn't waking up feeling so hopeless, and I was actually eating a bit better. I had started making those big pots of chili again. My sister taught me how to make it—she puts just a little bit of cocoa powder in the pot. Sounds strange, I know, but it really deepens the flavor. She moved out to Ohio back in '08, right near Cleveland. I took a Greyhound bus out there once to visit, and let me tell you, those buses are not built for comfort. My knees were aching for days. The driver was this older fella who kept playing old Willie Nelson tapes the whole way... 

But, uh, what was I saying? Oh, right. Even during those weeks when my mood lifted and I was doing okay, I still knew the neighbors were watching my door. I still knew they were reporting on me. Feeling better didn't change the fact that they were out there doing that.
Before all this started, did you have any major medical illness or head injury?

No, no major medical stuff, and I haven't bumped my head or anything like that. Well, I mean, I did scrape my elbow pretty bad last winter when I slipped on the ice outside the corner store. They never shovel that sidewalk right. The guy who runs it, Mr. Patel, he's always inside drinking tea out of this little thermos. It's one of those old plaid thermoses, the kind my dad used to take to the factory. Dad worked at the bottling plant for thirty years, stamping caps. He used to bring home these glass bottles that had misprints on the labels... but no, my head is fine. No medical problems like that.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is around?

Voices? No, I don't... I don't hear anything like that. Just the usual sounds around the apartment, you know? The radiator clanking. That thing makes a racket every time the heat kicks on. Sounds like somebody hitting a pipe with a wrench. My landlord, Gary, he keeps saying he's gonna bring a guy in to bleed the valves, but he never does. Gary's always too busy fixing up that old Chevy Nova he's got parked in the back alley. It's a '72, I think. Painted this awful mustard yellow color. He says he's gonna take it to car shows when it's done, but it's been sitting on blocks since before the pandemic. I told him he ought to just sell it for scrap, but he got real defensive about it. He's a sensitive guy, Gary. But no, no voices. Just the radiator and Gary's car radio when he's out there tinkering.
How long have you been convinced that your neighbors are watching you and sending notes about you?

Well, let's see... it's been a while now. I'd say it's been about a year and a month since I really noticed them watching me and slipping those notes around the office and the apartment. A year and a month. That would mean it started right around the time the old bakery on the corner closed down. You know, they used to make these incredible bear claws. Huge things, bigger than your hand, with all this sliced almond on top and just drowning in glaze. The lady who ran it, Mrs. Gable, she was a sweetheart. Always gave me an extra one if I came in right before closing. She had this little poodle that used to sit behind the counter, wearing a little red sweater in the winter. The dog's name was Barnaby. But then her rent went up, and she had to pack it all in. Now it's one of those fancy coffee shops where they charge you five dollars for a cup of black coffee, and the chairs are all made of metal so you can't even sit comfortably. I went in there once and asked for a bear claw, and the kid behind the counter looked at me like I had two heads. He had this little mustache, you know, one of those ones that twirls up at the ends... but yeah, about a year and a month since I started noticing the neighbors doing all that.
Do people ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or that you go off track when you talk?

Well, yeah, sometimes people do say that. Like, when I try to explain things, I'll start off talking about the rent, and then somehow I'm talking about the marina, and then the choir robes, and the wires in the walls, and people just look at me like I skipped half the story. It's like they can't keep up. The marina down by the lake, though, that place is really going downhill. Used to be you could rent a little aluminum rowboat for ten bucks for the whole afternoon. My buddy Dale and I used to go out there and fish for crappie. Dale had this tackle box that was older than I am, rusty green metal, and it always smelled like old bait and motor oil. He lost half his index finger in a table saw accident back in the eighties, but he could still tie a fishing knot faster than anyone I ever met. He moved down to Florida a few years back, lives in one of those retirement parks with the manufactured homes. Says the humidity is terrible for his arthritis, but he likes being near his grandkids. His oldest grandson plays the tuba in the high school marching band. Those uniforms they wear look so heavy, especially in the heat... but yeah, people do say I get off track and they can't follow what I'm saying sometimes.
Do you believe anyone is putting thoughts into your mind or taking thoughts out of your mind?

Putting thoughts in? Taking them out? No, no, nobody's doing that. That sounds like something out of one of those old science fiction movies. You know, the ones they used to show on channel 11 on Saturday afternoons? "Creature Double Feature," they called it. The host was this guy in a cheap vampire cape who always held a rubber bat. I used to watch those with my brother, Tommy. Tommy was crazy about monsters. He had this whole collection of those plastic models you had to glue together and paint yourself. The Wolfman, Frankenstein, the Mummy. He spent hours getting the paint just right on the Mummy's bandages. Used a little toothpick to get the dirt in the cracks so it looked real. He kept them all on this shelf above his bed, and my mother hated dusting in there because she was afraid she'd knock one over and break it. Tommy ended up working at a hardware store out in Ohio. Sells lawnmowers and snowblowers now. He says the winters out there are brutal, not like here. They get lake-effect snow that buries the cars overnight. He had to buy a special heavy-duty shovel just to get to his driveway... but no, I don't have anybody messing with my thoughts like that. Just my own thoughts in there.
Have people told you that your face or voice seems less expressive than it used to be?

No, nobody's really said anything like that to me. My voice is just my voice, I guess. It's not like I'm trying to be an announcer or anything. I used to love listening to those old radio announcers, though. Late at night, you'd get those AM stations coming in from hundreds of miles away, guys with those really deep, smooth voices. I had this silver Panasonic radio with a telescoping antenna that got bent when my buddy Phil sat on it. Phil was a big guy, worked down at the freight yards. He used to bring home these heavy wooden pallets and break them down for firewood. We'd sit out back and have a fire, maybe roast some hot dogs. You can't beat a hot dog cooked over real wood, gets that nice char on the outside. We used those cheap buns, though, the ones that fall apart the second you put mustard on them. I always liked the spicy brown mustard, not that bright yellow stuff. The yellow stuff stains your shirts, and I ruined a perfectly good flannel that way once. Had a tear in the elbow anyway, but still... what were we talking about? Oh, right, my face and voice. No, no one's told me I'm less expressive or anything like that.
Do you believe your neighbors are able to do anything impossible, like control events from a distance or use special devices to monitor you?

Well, they don't have special devices or anything crazy like that, but I know they're watching me. The people at my apartment building, I mean. I came in because I know they're keeping track of my comings and goings, always peeking out when I walk down the hall. And they're slipping notes about me to the front office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices they tape to the doors, like for water shut-offs or pest control. They had the exterminator come out last month because the lady in 4B said she saw a roach. Big water bugs, really, not the German kind. The German ones are the ones that really infest a place, get into the appliances and everything. My uncle Ray had an apartment in Chicago back in the seventies that got so bad he had to throw out his toaster. He said you'd turn it on and it would smell like burnt hair. He ended up moving out to the suburbs after that, bought a little brick ranch house. Had a nice yard, too, planted a bunch of tomato plants along the fence. Beefsteaks, I think they were. You slice one of those thick, put a little salt and pepper on it, maybe some mayonnaise on white bread... best sandwich in the world. But yeah, those notes on the doors, I know they're really about me, no matter what anyone says.
Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

Energetic? No, not really. I'm usually pretty tired, honestly. Never had a time where I didn't need sleep. Sleep's important, you know? My grandfather always used to say that an hour of sleep before midnight is worth two after. He worked the third shift at the bottling plant for thirty years, so he knew all about messing up his sleep schedule. He'd come home right when the sun was coming up, and my grandmother would have to pull these heavy, dark green curtains shut so he could get some rest. They were made of this really thick velvet material. She bought them at a discount store that used to be downtown, right next to the old movie theater. The theater got torn down back in the eighties to make room for a parking garage. It was a shame, too, because it had this beautiful marquee with all these flashing lightbulbs. They don't make signs like that anymore. Everything's digital now, just big screens everywhere you look. I saw a billboard the other day that changed pictures every ten seconds. It was advertising a car dealership, then a lawyer, then some kind of new energy drink. Those energy drinks can't be good for your heart, all that caffeine and sugar. I stick to coffee, mostly. Just black coffee. But anyway, no, I've never felt like I had too much energy or didn't need to sleep. I just feel worn out most of the time.
For at least six months, have you had these problems with people watching you and sending notes about you?

Six months? No, it's been longer than that. It's been about a year and a month now, dealing with them watching me and the notes and everything. I know exactly how long because it started right around the time the transmission went out on my old Buick. Just clunked out right in the middle of the intersection over by the hardware store. 

That hardware store's been there since I was a kid, you know. You go in there and it has that specific smell... like sawdust and fertilizer mixed together. They used to have this old golden retriever that just slept by the front door. You'd have to step right over him to get to the paint aisle. Paint's gotten so expensive lately, too. I was looking at a can of white semi-gloss a while back just to touch up the baseboards, and I couldn't believe the price. Used to be you could get a gallon for a few bucks. My dad was a house painter for a little while, back in the seventies. He always wore these white overalls that were just covered in every color imaginable. He looked like a modern art painting himself by the time he got home. He'd leave his boots on the porch so he wouldn't track it in... 

But, uh, yeah. To answer your question, it's been a year and a month since all this stuff with the neighbors started.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Well, yeah, I guess I have. I used to look forward to a lot of things, really. Choir practice on Wednesdays, playing bridge with the guys, even just cooking up a big pot of beans on Sunday... I used to do little repair jobs for folks around the building, too, fixing leaky faucets or patching drywall. But now, I just mostly let the phone ring. I tell myself there's no point in going or doing any of it. 

I used to be real handy, you know. I had this big red toolbox my brother gave me for my birthday one year. It had all these little compartments on top for screws and nails, kept everything sorted. Sorting things used to be real calming for me. I'd sit at the kitchen table and organize all my hardware by size. My brother, he moved out to Arizona about ten years ago. Said he couldn't take the winters here anymore. He bought a house out in the desert, said he doesn't even have to mow the lawn because it's all rocks and cactus. Sounds kind of nice, not having to worry about yard work. Mowers can be a real hassle when the carburetor gets gunked up. You gotta take the whole thing apart and soak it in carburetor cleaner... smells awful, that stuff. Gives you a headache if you don't do it in a well-ventilated area. But yeah, I just don't have the energy or the care for any of my old hobbies anymore. Just seems pointless.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you still believed your neighbors were watching you and sending notes about you, but you were not feeling depressed at all?

Yeah, there was. There was a spell of several weeks, maybe a month or so ago, where I was actually eating a bit better. Woke up not feeling quite so... heavy and hopeless, you know? But I still knew they were watching my door. Still knew they were reporting on me. 

Speaking of doors, my front door has this squeak that just won't quit. It's the bottom hinge. I've tried WD-40, I've tried rubbing a bar of soap on it—my mom used to swear by that trick for squeaky floorboards. She had this old house with these original hardwood floors that groaned every time you took a step. It was impossible to sneak down to the kitchen for a midnight snack when I was a kid. She'd always catch me. She'd be sitting there in the dark, drinking a glass of warm milk. Said it helped her sleep. I never understood how people could drink warm milk, it just coats your throat in this weird way. But she liked it. She always had it in this chipped blue mug with a little white sailboat painted on it. I wonder whatever happened to that mug... probably got lost in the shuffle when we cleaned out her house. It's funny the things you hold onto and the things that just slip away. But yeah, even when I was feeling a bit more normal, eating alright and not so down, I still knew they had their eyes on me and were sending those notes.
Have you ever felt that outside forces were controlling your actions?

Outside forces? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm the one moving my own arms and legs, you know? I do what I decide to do. 

Speaking of legs, though, my left knee has been acting up lately whenever it rains. Just aches right down to the bone. Reminds me of when I fell off the roof of my buddy Al's garage back in '88. We were trying to fix the shingles before a big storm rolled in. Black clouds just sitting over the whole neighborhood, looked like the end of the world. Al had this old Ford pickup truck parked in the driveway, a real beauty, cherry red. He used to spend every Saturday polishing that thing until you could see your reflection in the bumper. Chrome bumpers... they don't make 'em like that anymore. Now everything's just plastic and fiberglass on cars. If you get into a fender bender nowadays, the whole front end just crumbles like a soda can. Used to be you could just take a rubber mallet and pound a dent right out yourself. I had a really good rubber mallet, actually... heavy wooden handle. Left it in the trunk of that Buick I was telling you about earlier. Shame to lose a good tool.
Besides your neighbors watching you and sending notes, have you had any other strong beliefs that other people said were not true?

Well, no, not really other things. It's just... I came in here because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. They're slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices on the doors, like for pest control or whatever, but I know what they're really doing. 

Pest control, though... they came by a few months ago spraying for roaches. Used this stuff that smelled like burnt tires. Reminded me of when I worked at the junkyard for a bit, back in my twenties. We'd have these huge piles of tires, mountains of them. Sometimes in the summer, the heat would just bake the rubber and the smell would hang over the whole lot. We had this big guard dog there, a Rottweiler mix named Buster. Meanest looking dog you ever saw, but he was a total softie if you had a piece of beef jerky. I used to buy those long sticks of jerky from the gas station on the corner. The guy who ran the place, Sal, he always gave me a discount because I helped him fix his cash register once. It was one of those old mechanical ones with the heavy keys that make a real loud *cha-ching* sound. You don't hear that sound anymore. Now it's all just beeps and touchscreens. You can't even feel the buttons. I like to feel a button when I press it, you know? Makes you feel like you've actually done something. But yeah, everybody says it's just notices on the doors, but I know they're keeping track of me.
When you talk, do your thoughts ever get so jumbled that you feel they don’t connect logically?

Well, yeah, sometimes I guess they do. Like, I'll be trying to explain something to somebody, and I start off talking about the rent being due, and then somehow I'm talking about the marina down by the lake, and then the old choir robes from church, and then the wires they put in the walls... and people just look at me like I skipped half the story. 

Speaking of the marina, I used to go down there and just watch the boats come in. There was this one guy, Captain Dan they called him, he had a pontoon boat that he rigged up with a grill right on the deck. He'd be out there flipping burgers while he was steering. Smelled so good, especially on a Tuesday afternoon when it wasn't too crowded. Tuesdays are always the best day to go to the grocery store, too. They restock the shelves on Monday nights, so everything is fresh. I always get the iceberg lettuce because it stays crunchy longer than that leafy green stuff. You ever try to make a sandwich with soggy lettuce? Ruins the whole thing. A good sandwich needs a firm foundation. My grandma used to make the best sandwiches, always on rye bread with a thick slice of tomato from her garden. She had these huge tomato plants, practically trees. She used to tie them up with old strips of pantyhose to keep them from falling over. Pantyhose are surprisingly strong, you know. But yeah, people look at me like I'm not making sense when I try to explain things.
Do you ever feel that other people can hear or know your thoughts, even when you haven’t said them out loud?

Hear my thoughts? No, I don't think anyone can do that. I mean, they're inside my head, behind the bone, you know? Unless they've got some kind of machine, but I haven't seen anything like that. 

Machines are getting pretty crazy these days, though. I saw this thing on the TV the other day, a commercial for a refrigerator that tells you when you're out of milk. Now, why do I need a refrigerator to tell me that? I just open the door and look. It's got a whole screen on the front of it, like a computer. Computers are everywhere now. I remember when they first started putting them in the library downtown. Big clunky things with green letters on the screen. The librarian, Mrs. Gable, she hated them. She said they ruined the quiet. She was a real stickler for quiet. If you even coughed too loud, she'd give you this look over her glasses that would freeze you right in your tracks. She wore those glasses on a little chain around her neck, pearl chain. My aunt had a chain like that for her glasses, but hers was gold. Real gold, she said, but I think it was just plated because it started turning green after a few years. Turned her neck green, too, right where it rested. She used to scrub it with a washcloth and some of that harsh orange soap they use in garages. Smells like citrus, but it's got grit in it. Good for getting grease off your hands if you've been working on an engine. I haven't worked on an engine in years, though. But no, nobody's listening to what's in my head.
Has your mind ever seemed to stop in the middle of a sentence so that you suddenly couldn’t continue what you were saying?

Stop in the middle? No, I don't think my mind just stops like that. I usually just keep going until I'm done saying what I need to say. 

Speaking of stopping, though, the brakes on my old Ford used to do that. Just lock right up if you hit 'em too hard. I had this '82 pickup, powder blue, rust around the wheel wells. I used to drive it down to the hardware store on Saturday mornings. The guy there, Earl, he always had a pot of coffee going in the back room. Strong stuff, tasted like it had been sitting there since Tuesday. But he'd pour you a cup in one of those styrofoam cups if you bought something. Styrofoam is terrible for the environment, you know. They say it takes a million years to break down in a landfill. Just sits there, taking up space. Kind of like those old encyclopedias I have in my closet. A whole set, A to Z, from 1995. Bought them from a door-to-door salesman. You don't see door-to-door salesmen anymore. Used to be guys selling vacuums, brushes, encyclopedias. He had this nice suit on, but his shoes were scuffed up real bad. You can always tell a lot about a man by his shoes. My dad always said, "Keep your shoes shined and your watch wound." He had this old pocket watch, silver, with a train engraved on the front. It ticked so loud you could hear it across the room. Tick, tick, tick... very steady. But no, my mind doesn't just stop in the middle of a sentence.
Have these problems made it hard for you to manage everyday things like work, paying bills, cooking, or taking care of yourself?

Well, yeah, it’s gotten pretty bad. I’ve fallen way behind on my bills, and I keep missing my appointments. I even stopped showing up for church and the volunteering I used to do because I just can't keep my days organized anymore, and I don't really trust talking to people right now. 

Speaking of bills, the electric company sent me a letter on this pink paper last week. Why pink? It used to be white with a little red stamp, but now it’s this bright pink. Reminds me of the cotton candy they used to sell at the county fair. We used to go every August when the weather was so hot you could fry an egg on the sidewalk. They had this guy who would spin the sugar right in front of you, huge clouds of it on a paper cone. I always got the blue kind, tastes like blue raspberry. Raspberries are hard to grow, though. The bushes get all thorny and tangled if you don't prune them back in the late winter. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he tried growing them along the fence line, but the birds got to them before they ever ripened. He put up this fake owl to scare them away, plastic thing with big yellow eyes. It worked for a week, and then the crows just started sitting right on its head. Crows are smart birds, they figure things out quick. They like shiny things, too. I read once they collect bottle caps and bits of foil for their nests. Foil is getting thinner these days, you notice that? You try to wrap a baked potato and it just tears right down the middle. But yeah, I can't really manage my days or the bills or any of that stuff lately.

patient.answer: Well, I wouldn't say high or energized. I don't really get like that. But depressed... yeah. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day already went bad before I even get my feet on the floor. It's just this weight. My mattress doesn't help either, it's one of those old spring ones. I bought it at a discount place over on 4th Street, you know the one with the big yellow sign? The guy there told me it was firm, but I think he just wanted to make a sale. He had this little dog behind the counter, a terrier mix, I think. Reminded me of a dog I had when I was a kid, Buster. Buster used to chase the mail truck every single day... but yeah, I just feel so down and empty most days.

patient.answer:
Yeah, actually... there was a spell a little while back. It lasted for several weeks, I think. I wasn't waking up feeling so hopeless, and I was actually eating a bit better. I had started making those big pots of chili again. My sister taught me how to make it—she puts just a little bit of cocoa powder in the pot. Sounds strange, I know, but it really deepens the flavor. She moved out to Ohio back in '08, right near Cleveland. I took a Greyhound bus out there once to visit, and let me tell you, those buses are not built for comfort. My knees were aching for days. The driver was this older fella who kept playing old Willie Nelson tapes the whole way... 

But, uh, what was I saying? Oh, right. Even during those weeks when my mood lifted and I was doing okay, I still knew the neighbors were watching my door. I still knew they were reporting on me. Feeling better didn't change the fact that they were out there doing that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms are due to a medical or neurological condition rather than a primary psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: Before all this started, did you have any major medical illness or head injury?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about major medical illnesses or head injuries to rule out organic causes, which is not covered by any of the items in the symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, no major medical stuff, and I haven't bumped my head or anything like that. Well, I mean, I did scrape my elbow pretty bad last winter when I slipped on the ice outside the corner store. They never shovel that sidewalk right. The guy who runs it, Mr. Patel, he's always inside drinking tea out of this little thermos. It's one of those old plaid thermoses, the kind my dad used to take to the factory. Dad worked at the bottling plant for thirty years, stamping caps. He used to bring home these glass bottles that had misprints on the labels... but no, my head is fine. No medical problems like that.

inference.note: Ruled out F06.2 because the patient denies major medical illness or head injury preceding symptom onset. Persistent persecutory delusions occur outside depressive periods, keeping F22 and F20.0 in the differential; F25.9 remains possible pending further characterization of mood episode proportion and other psychotic symptoms.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent hallucinations, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder and schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: Do you ever hear voices when no one else is around?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about auditory hallucinations (hearing voices), which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: Voices? No, I don't... I don't hear anything like that. Just the usual sounds around the apartment, you know? The radiator clanking. That thing makes a racket every time the heat kicks on. Sounds like somebody hitting a pipe with a wrench. My landlord, Gary, he keeps saying he's gonna bring a guy in to bleed the valves, but he never does. Gary's always too busy fixing up that old Chevy Nova he's got parked in the back alley. It's a '72, I think. Painted this awful mustard yellow color. He says he's gonna take it to car shows when it's done, but it's been sitting on blocks since before the pandemic. I told him he ought to just sell it for scrap, but he got real defensive about it. He's a sensitive guy, Gary. But no, no voices. Just the radiator and Gary's car radio when he's out there tinkering.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have lasted at least one month, which best distinguishes delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum disorders at this point.
doctor.question: How long have you been convinced that your neighbors are watching you and sending notes about you?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The suspicious thoughts about the apartment neighbors and office have been with me for about a year and a month.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about how long the patient has been experiencing the delusional thoughts regarding the neighbors watching and reporting on him.

patient.answer: Well, let's see... it's been a while now. I'd say it's been about a year and a month since I really noticed them watching me and slipping those notes around the office and the apartment. A year and a month. That would mean it started right around the time the old bakery on the corner closed down. You know, they used to make these incredible bear claws. Huge things, bigger than your hand, with all this sliced almond on top and just drowning in glaze. The lady who ran it, Mrs. Gable, she was a sweetheart. Always gave me an extra one if I came in right before closing. She had this little poodle that used to sit behind the counter, wearing a little red sweater in the winter. The dog's name was Barnaby. But then her rent went up, and she had to pack it all in. Now it's one of those fancy coffee shops where they charge you five dollars for a cup of black coffee, and the chairs are all made of metal so you can't even sit comfortably. I went in there once and asked for a bear claw, and the kid behind the counter looked at me like I had two heads. He had this little mustache, you know, one of those ones that twirls up at the ends... but yeah, about a year and a month since I started noticing the neighbors doing all that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has prominent disorganized speech/thought disorder, which would favor schizophrenia over persistent delusional disorder and help separate the remaining diagnoses.
doctor.question: Do people ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or that you go off track when you talk?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
target_item.manifestation: When I try to explain things, I start with the rent, then the marina, then the choir robes and the wires in the walls, and people look at me like I skipped half the story.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if my speech is hard to follow or if I go off track, which directly addresses disorganized thinking and speech.

patient.answer: Well, yeah, sometimes people do say that. Like, when I try to explain things, I'll start off talking about the rent, and then somehow I'm talking about the marina, and then the choir robes, and the wires in the walls, and people just look at me like I skipped half the story. It's like they can't keep up. The marina down by the lake, though, that place is really going downhill. Used to be you could rent a little aluminum rowboat for ten bucks for the whole afternoon. My buddy Dale and I used to go out there and fish for crappie. Dale had this tackle box that was older than I am, rusty green metal, and it always smelled like old bait and motor oil. He lost half his index finger in a table saw accident back in the eighties, but he could still tie a fishing knot faster than anyone I ever met. He moved down to Florida a few years back, lives in one of those retirement parks with the manufactured homes. Says the humidity is terrible for his arthritis, but he likes being near his grandkids. His oldest grandson plays the tuba in the high school marching band. Those uniforms they wear look so heavy, especially in the heat... but yeah, people do say I get off track and they can't follow what I'm saying sometimes.

inference.note: This turn adds evidence of formal thought disorder/disorganized speech (frequently off track, hard to follow), which increases support for schizophrenia-spectrum illness, especially F20.0, while keeping F25.9 possible because depressive episodes are present but psychosis also occurs outside mood episodes. Persistent persecutory delusions without hallucinations still leave F22 on the differential, though disorganization makes it less favored.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has bizarre delusions or Schneiderian-type psychotic symptoms that would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Do you believe anyone is putting thoughts into your mind or taking thoughts out of your mind?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought insertion or thought withdrawal, which are specific types of delusions that are not part of my symptom profile.

patient.answer: Putting thoughts in? Taking them out? No, no, nobody's doing that. That sounds like something out of one of those old science fiction movies. You know, the ones they used to show on channel 11 on Saturday afternoons? "Creature Double Feature," they called it. The host was this guy in a cheap vampire cape who always held a rubber bat. I used to watch those with my brother, Tommy. Tommy was crazy about monsters. He had this whole collection of those plastic models you had to glue together and paint yourself. The Wolfman, Frankenstein, the Mummy. He spent hours getting the paint just right on the Mummy's bandages. Used a little toothpick to get the dirt in the cracks so it looked real. He kept them all on this shelf above his bed, and my mother hated dusting in there because she was afraid she'd knock one over and break it. Tommy ended up working at a hardware store out in Ohio. Sells lawnmowers and snowblowers now. He says the winters out there are brutal, not like here. They get lake-effect snow that buries the cars overnight. He had to buy a special heavy-duty shovel just to get to his driveway... but no, I don't have anybody messing with my thoughts like that. Just my own thoughts in there.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are negative symptoms, especially reduced emotional expression, to help distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder or schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: Have people told you that your face or voice seems less expressive than it used to be?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about diminished emotional expression (affective flattening), which is a negative symptom of schizophrenia. This is not included in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, nobody's really said anything like that to me. My voice is just my voice, I guess. It's not like I'm trying to be an announcer or anything. I used to love listening to those old radio announcers, though. Late at night, you'd get those AM stations coming in from hundreds of miles away, guys with those really deep, smooth voices. I had this silver Panasonic radio with a telescoping antenna that got bent when my buddy Phil sat on it. Phil was a big guy, worked down at the freight yards. He used to bring home these heavy wooden pallets and break them down for firewood. We'd sit out back and have a fire, maybe roast some hot dogs. You can't beat a hot dog cooked over real wood, gets that nice char on the outside. We used those cheap buns, though, the ones that fall apart the second you put mustard on them. I always liked the spicy brown mustard, not that bright yellow stuff. The yellow stuff stains your shirts, and I ruined a perfectly good flannel that way once. Had a tear in the elbow anyway, but still... what were we talking about? Oh, right, my face and voice. No, no one's told me I'm less expressive or anything like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is bizarre, which best distinguishes schizophrenia from delusional disorder given the absence of mood congruence and unclear schizoaffective features.
doctor.question: Do you believe your neighbors are able to do anything impossible, like control events from a distance or use special devices to monitor you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings and slipping notes about me to the office, even though everybody keeps telling me it's just notices on the doors.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about delusions of being monitored or controlled by neighbors, which corresponds to my symptom of believing the people at my apartment are watching me and reporting on me.

patient.answer: Well, they don't have special devices or anything crazy like that, but I know they're watching me. The people at my apartment building, I mean. I came in because I know they're keeping track of my comings and goings, always peeking out when I walk down the hall. And they're slipping notes about me to the front office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices they tape to the doors, like for water shut-offs or pest control. They had the exterminator come out last month because the lady in 4B said she saw a roach. Big water bugs, really, not the German kind. The German ones are the ones that really infest a place, get into the appliances and everything. My uncle Ray had an apartment in Chicago back in the seventies that got so bad he had to throw out his toaster. He said you'd turn it on and it would smell like burnt hair. He ended up moving out to the suburbs after that, bought a little brick ranch house. Had a nice yard, too, planted a bunch of tomato plants along the fence. Beefsteaks, I think they were. You slice one of those thick, put a little salt and pepper on it, maybe some mayonnaise on white bread... best sandwich in the world. But yeah, those notes on the doors, I know they're really about me, no matter what anyone says.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a manic episode, which would strongly favor schizoaffective disorder over schizophrenia or delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of a manic or hypomanic episode (feeling unusually energetic, decreased need for sleep), which is not part of my symptom profile (Depressive Type).

patient.answer: Energetic? No, not really. I'm usually pretty tired, honestly. Never had a time where I didn't need sleep. Sleep's important, you know? My grandfather always used to say that an hour of sleep before midnight is worth two after. He worked the third shift at the bottling plant for thirty years, so he knew all about messing up his sleep schedule. He'd come home right when the sun was coming up, and my grandmother would have to pull these heavy, dark green curtains shut so he could get some rest. They were made of this really thick velvet material. She bought them at a discount store that used to be downtown, right next to the old movie theater. The theater got torn down back in the eighties to make room for a parking garage. It was a shame, too, because it had this beautiful marquee with all these flashing lightbulbs. They don't make signs like that anymore. Everything's digital now, just big screens everywhere you look. I saw a billboard the other day that changed pictures every ten seconds. It was advertising a car dealership, then a lawyer, then some kind of new energy drink. Those energy drinks can't be good for your heart, all that caffeine and sugar. I stick to coffee, mostly. Just black coffee. But anyway, no, I've never felt like I had too much energy or didn't need to sleep. I just feel worn out most of the time.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have persisted for at least six months, which helps distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder and schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: For at least six months, have you had these problems with people watching you and sending notes about you?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The suspicious thoughts about the apartment neighbors and office have been with me for about a year and a month.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of my specific psychotic symptoms (the delusions about people watching me and sending notes), which matches the Psychotic Symptoms Duration item in my profile.

patient.answer:
Six months? No, it's been longer than that. It's been about a year and a month now, dealing with them watching me and the notes and everything. I know exactly how long because it started right around the time the transmission went out on my old Buick. Just clunked out right in the middle of the intersection over by the hardware store. 

That hardware store's been there since I was a kid, you know. You go in there and it has that specific smell... like sawdust and fertilizer mixed together. They used to have this old golden retriever that just slept by the front door. You'd have to step right over him to get to the paint aisle. Paint's gotten so expensive lately, too. I was looking at a can of white semi-gloss a while back just to touch up the baseboards, and I couldn't believe the price. Used to be you could get a gallon for a few bucks. My dad was a house painter for a little while, back in the seventies. He always wore these white overalls that were just covered in every color imaginable. He looked like a modern art painting himself by the time he got home. He'd leave his boots on the porch so he wouldn't track it in... 

But, uh, yeah. To answer your question, it's been a year and a month since all this stuff with the neighbors started.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has prominent negative symptoms, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder and help separate it from schizoaffective disorder given the already excluded mania and unclear depressive syndrome.
doctor.question: Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I used to look forward to choir practice, bridge, cooking beans on Sunday, and doing little repair jobs for folks, but now I mostly let the phone ring and tell myself there is no point going.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking if I have lost interest in activities I used to enjoy, which maps to the Loss of Interest symptom.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, I guess I have. I used to look forward to a lot of things, really. Choir practice on Wednesdays, playing bridge with the guys, even just cooking up a big pot of beans on Sunday... I used to do little repair jobs for folks around the building, too, fixing leaky faucets or patching drywall. But now, I just mostly let the phone ring. I tell myself there's no point in going or doing any of it. 

I used to be real handy, you know. I had this big red toolbox my brother gave me for my birthday one year. It had all these little compartments on top for screws and nails, kept everything sorted. Sorting things used to be real calming for me. I'd sit at the kitchen table and organize all my hardware by size. My brother, he moved out to Arizona about ten years ago. Said he couldn't take the winters here anymore. He bought a house out in the desert, said he doesn't even have to mow the lawn because it's all rocks and cactus. Sounds kind of nice, not having to worry about yard work. Mowers can be a real hassle when the carburetor gets gunked up. You gotta take the whole thing apart and soak it in carburetor cleaner... smells awful, that stuff. Gives you a headache if you don't do it in a well-ventilated area. But yeah, I just don't have the energy or the care for any of my old hobbies anymore. Just seems pointless.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there have been at least two weeks of psychotic symptoms in the absence of any mood episode, which would distinguish schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia or delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you still believed your neighbors were watching you and sending notes about you, but you were not feeling depressed at all?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There was a spell of several weeks when I was eating a bit better and not waking up so hopeless, but I still believed the neighbors were watching my door and reporting on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the delusions (neighbors watching and sending notes) occurred for at least two weeks without feeling depressed, which directly corresponds to Criterion B (psychotic symptoms in the absence of a major mood episode).

patient.answer:
Yeah, there was. There was a spell of several weeks, maybe a month or so ago, where I was actually eating a bit better. Woke up not feeling quite so... heavy and hopeless, you know? But I still knew they were watching my door. Still knew they were reporting on me. 

Speaking of doors, my front door has this squeak that just won't quit. It's the bottom hinge. I've tried WD-40, I've tried rubbing a bar of soap on it—my mom used to swear by that trick for squeaky floorboards. She had this old house with these original hardwood floors that groaned every time you took a step. It was impossible to sneak down to the kitchen for a midnight snack when I was a kid. She'd always catch me. She'd be sitting there in the dark, drinking a glass of warm milk. Said it helped her sleep. I never understood how people could drink warm milk, it just coats your throat in this weird way. But she liked it. She always had it in this chipped blue mug with a little white sailboat painted on it. I wonder whatever happened to that mug... probably got lost in the shuffle when we cleaned out her house. It's funny the things you hold onto and the things that just slip away. But yeah, even when I was feeling a bit more normal, eating alright and not so down, I still knew they had their eyes on me and were sending those notes.

doctor.intent: Determine whether bizarre delusions or Schneiderian first-rank psychotic symptoms are present, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder and help distinguish from schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that outside forces were controlling your actions?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about delusions of control (outside forces controlling actions), which is not part of the patient's symptom profile. The patient's delusions (S019) are persecutory in nature (being watched and reported on), not related to being controlled.

patient.answer:
Outside forces? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm the one moving my own arms and legs, you know? I do what I decide to do. 

Speaking of legs, though, my left knee has been acting up lately whenever it rains. Just aches right down to the bone. Reminds me of when I fell off the roof of my buddy Al's garage back in '88. We were trying to fix the shingles before a big storm rolled in. Black clouds just sitting over the whole neighborhood, looked like the end of the world. Al had this old Ford pickup truck parked in the driveway, a real beauty, cherry red. He used to spend every Saturday polishing that thing until you could see your reflection in the bumper. Chrome bumpers... they don't make 'em like that anymore. Now everything's just plastic and fiberglass on cars. If you get into a fender bender nowadays, the whole front end just crumbles like a soda can. Used to be you could just take a rubber mallet and pound a dent right out yourself. I had a really good rubber mallet, actually... heavy wooden handle. Left it in the trunk of that Buick I was telling you about earlier. Shame to lose a good tool.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the long-standing persecutory belief is accompanied by other bizarre delusions, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Besides your neighbors watching you and sending notes, have you had any other strong beliefs that other people said were not true?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings and slipping notes about me to the office, even though everybody keeps telling me it's just notices on the doors.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I have any other strong, fixed beliefs that others think are untrue, which is an inquiry about other potential delusions.

patient.answer:
Well, no, not really other things. It's just... I came in here because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. They're slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices on the doors, like for pest control or whatever, but I know what they're really doing. 

Pest control, though... they came by a few months ago spraying for roaches. Used this stuff that smelled like burnt tires. Reminded me of when I worked at the junkyard for a bit, back in my twenties. We'd have these huge piles of tires, mountains of them. Sometimes in the summer, the heat would just bake the rubber and the smell would hang over the whole lot. We had this big guard dog there, a Rottweiler mix named Buster. Meanest looking dog you ever saw, but he was a total softie if you had a piece of beef jerky. I used to buy those long sticks of jerky from the gas station on the corner. The guy who ran the place, Sal, he always gave me a discount because I helped him fix his cash register once. It was one of those old mechanical ones with the heavy keys that make a real loud *cha-ching* sound. You don't hear that sound anymore. Now it's all just beeps and touchscreens. You can't even feel the buttons. I like to feel a button when I press it, you know? Makes you feel like you've actually done something. But yeah, everybody says it's just notices on the doors, but I know they're keeping track of me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent formal thought-disorder symptoms beyond circumstantiality/tangentiality, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: When you talk, do your thoughts ever get so jumbled that you feel they don’t connect logically?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
target_item.manifestation: When I try to explain things, I start with the rent, then the marina, then the choir robes and the wires in the walls, and people look at me like I skipped half the story.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if my thoughts get jumbled and don't connect logically, which directly relates to disorganized thinking and speech.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, sometimes I guess they do. Like, I'll be trying to explain something to somebody, and I start off talking about the rent being due, and then somehow I'm talking about the marina down by the lake, and then the old choir robes from church, and then the wires they put in the walls... and people just look at me like I skipped half the story. 

Speaking of the marina, I used to go down there and just watch the boats come in. There was this one guy, Captain Dan they called him, he had a pontoon boat that he rigged up with a grill right on the deck. He'd be out there flipping burgers while he was steering. Smelled so good, especially on a Tuesday afternoon when it wasn't too crowded. Tuesdays are always the best day to go to the grocery store, too. They restock the shelves on Monday nights, so everything is fresh. I always get the iceberg lettuce because it stays crunchy longer than that leafy green stuff. You ever try to make a sandwich with soggy lettuce? Ruins the whole thing. A good sandwich needs a firm foundation. My grandma used to make the best sandwiches, always on rye bread with a thick slice of tomato from her garden. She had these huge tomato plants, practically trees. She used to tie them up with old strips of pantyhose to keep them from falling over. Pantyhose are surprisingly strong, you know. But yeah, people look at me like I'm not making sense when I try to explain things.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the thought disorder includes Schneiderian first-rank symptom of thought broadcasting, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder and help distinguish from schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: Do you ever feel that other people can hear or know your thoughts, even when you haven’t said them out loud?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought broadcasting, a specific type of delusion. The patient's symptom profile only includes persecutory delusions (being watched/reported on), not thought broadcasting.

patient.answer:
Hear my thoughts? No, I don't think anyone can do that. I mean, they're inside my head, behind the bone, you know? Unless they've got some kind of machine, but I haven't seen anything like that. 

Machines are getting pretty crazy these days, though. I saw this thing on the TV the other day, a commercial for a refrigerator that tells you when you're out of milk. Now, why do I need a refrigerator to tell me that? I just open the door and look. It's got a whole screen on the front of it, like a computer. Computers are everywhere now. I remember when they first started putting them in the library downtown. Big clunky things with green letters on the screen. The librarian, Mrs. Gable, she hated them. She said they ruined the quiet. She was a real stickler for quiet. If you even coughed too loud, she'd give you this look over her glasses that would freeze you right in your tracks. She wore those glasses on a little chain around her neck, pearl chain. My aunt had a chain like that for her glasses, but hers was gold. Real gold, she said, but I think it was just plated because it started turning green after a few years. Turned her neck green, too, right where it rested. She used to scrub it with a washcloth and some of that harsh orange soap they use in garages. Smells like citrus, but it's got grit in it. Good for getting grease off your hands if you've been working on an engine. I haven't worked on an engine in years, though. But no, nobody's listening to what's in my head.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the disorganized speech represents a persistent schizophrenia-spectrum thought disorder severe enough to distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder, given mood episodes do not account for the psychosis.
doctor.question: Has your mind ever seemed to stop in the middle of a sentence so that you suddenly couldn’t continue what you were saying?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought blocking (suddenly stopping in the middle of a sentence/thought), which is not present in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Stop in the middle? No, I don't think my mind just stops like that. I usually just keep going until I'm done saying what I need to say. 

Speaking of stopping, though, the brakes on my old Ford used to do that. Just lock right up if you hit 'em too hard. I had this '82 pickup, powder blue, rust around the wheel wells. I used to drive it down to the hardware store on Saturday mornings. The guy there, Earl, he always had a pot of coffee going in the back room. Strong stuff, tasted like it had been sitting there since Tuesday. But he'd pour you a cup in one of those styrofoam cups if you bought something. Styrofoam is terrible for the environment, you know. They say it takes a million years to break down in a landfill. Just sits there, taking up space. Kind of like those old encyclopedias I have in my closet. A whole set, A to Z, from 1995. Bought them from a door-to-door salesman. You don't see door-to-door salesmen anymore. Used to be guys selling vacuums, brushes, encyclopedias. He had this nice suit on, but his shoes were scuffed up real bad. You can always tell a lot about a man by his shoes. My dad always said, "Keep your shoes shined and your watch wound." He had this old pocket watch, silver, with a train engraved on the front. It ticked so loud you could hear it across the room. Tick, tick, tick... very steady. But no, my mind doesn't just stop in the middle of a sentence.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the disorganized speech reflects a broader functional decline outside the fixed delusion, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have these problems made it hard for you to manage everyday things like work, paying bills, cooking, or taking care of yourself?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I have fallen behind on bills, missed appointments, and stopped showing up for church and volunteer commitments because I cannot keep my days organized or trust ordinary interactions.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the symptoms have made it difficult to manage everyday tasks, work, paying bills, cooking, or self-care, which directly maps to functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, it’s gotten pretty bad. I’ve fallen way behind on my bills, and I keep missing my appointments. I even stopped showing up for church and the volunteering I used to do because I just can't keep my days organized anymore, and I don't really trust talking to people right now. 

Speaking of bills, the electric company sent me a letter on this pink paper last week. Why pink? It used to be white with a little red stamp, but now it’s this bright pink. Reminds me of the cotton candy they used to sell at the county fair. We used to go every August when the weather was so hot you could fry an egg on the sidewalk. They had this guy who would spin the sugar right in front of you, huge clouds of it on a paper cone. I always got the blue kind, tastes like blue raspberry. Raspberries are hard to grow, though. The bushes get all thorny and tangled if you don't prune them back in the late winter. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he tried growing them along the fence line, but the birds got to them before they ever ripened. He put up this fake owl to scare them away, plastic thing with big yellow eyes. It worked for a week, and then the crows just started sitting right on its head. Crows are smart birds, they figure things out quick. They like shiny things, too. I read once they collect bottle caps and bits of foil for their nests. Foil is getting thinner these days, you notice that? You try to wrap a baked potato and it just tears right down the middle. But yeah, I can't really manage my days or the bills or any of that stuff lately.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent non-bizarre persecutory delusion for over 1 year that neighbors are watching him and sending notes about him, with preserved denial of core Schneiderian symptoms such as thought insertion, thought withdrawal, thought broadcasting, and passivity experiences.
